---
title: "Fisher Information and Delta Method for the Toothpaste Cap Problem"
format: pdf
---

## Setup

For the \emph{toothpaste cap problem}, we have

$$
\ell(\pi)=\log L(\pi)
= k\log\pi+(N-k)\log(1-\pi)
$$

and

$$
\hat\pi=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N y_i = \operatorname{avg}(y)= \frac{k}{N}.
$$

To estimate the variance, we need

$$
\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat\pi)
\;\approx\;
\big[\mathcal I_{\text{obs}}(\hat\pi)\big]^{-1}
=
\left[
-\,\left.\frac{d^2 \ell(\pi)}{d\pi^2}\right|_{\pi=\hat\pi}
\right]^{-1}.
$$

\newpage

## Finding $\hat{\text{SE}}(\hat \pi)$

### Finding derivatives of $\ell$

The first derivative is $\frac{d\ell}{d\pi} = \frac{k}{\pi}-\frac{N-k}{1-\pi}$.

The second derivative is $\frac{d^2\ell}{d\pi^2} = -\frac{k}{\pi^{2}} -\frac{N-k}{(1-\pi)^{2}}$ (see below).



::: callout-note
## Some tedious algebra

\begin{align*}
\frac{d\ell}{d\pi}
  &= \frac{k}{\pi} - \frac{N-k}{1-\pi}, \\[8pt]
\frac{d^2\ell}{d\pi^2}
  &= \frac{d}{d\pi}\!\left(\frac{k}{\pi}\right) - \frac{d}{d\pi}\!\left(\frac{N-k}{1-\pi}\right)
   && \text{differentiate term by term} \\[4pt]
  &= k\,\frac{d}{d\pi}(\pi^{-1}) \;-\; (N-k)\,\frac{d}{d\pi}\big((1-\pi)^{-1}\big)
   && \text{rewrite as powers} \\[4pt]
  &= k(-1)\pi^{-2} \;-\; (N-k)\big[(-1)(1-\pi)^{-2}\cdot(-1)\big]
   && \text{power rule + chain rule} \\[4pt]
  &= -\frac{k}{\pi^{2}} \;-\; (N-k)(1-\pi)^{-2}
   \\[4pt]
  &= -\frac{k}{\pi^{2}} \;-\; \frac{N-k}{(1-\pi)^{2}}.
\end{align*}
:::

\newpage

### Simplifying $-\ell''(\hat \pi)$

Evaluate the negative second derivative at $\pi=\hat\pi$.

$$
-\left.\frac{d^2\ell}{d\pi^2}\right|_{\pi=\hat\pi} = \frac{N}{\hat\pi(1-\hat\pi)}
$$
Thus,

$$
\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat\pi)
\;\approx\;
\left[-\left.\frac{d^2\ell}{d\pi^2}\right|_{\pi=\hat\pi}\right]^{-1}
= \left[ \frac{N}{\hat\pi(1-\hat\pi)} \right]^{-1}
= \frac{\hat\pi(1-\hat\pi)}{N}
$$

and

$$
\boxed{\;
\widehat{\mathrm{SE}}(\hat\pi)
\approx \sqrt{\frac{\hat\pi(1-\hat\pi)}{N}}
\;}
$$

::: callout-note
## Some tedious algebra

Use the following identities:

-   $k = N\hat\pi$. → Multiply both sides of $\hat\pi = k/N$ by $N$.
-   $N-k = N(1-\hat\pi)$. → $N-k = N - (N \cdot k/N) = N - N\hat\pi = N(1-\hat\pi)$.
-   $\tfrac{1}{a}+\tfrac{1}{b} = \tfrac{a+b}{ab}$. → Common, useful identity.

\begin{align*}
-\left.\frac{d^2\ell}{d\pi^2}\right|_{\pi=\hat\pi}
&= \frac{k}{\hat\pi^2} + \frac{N-k}{(1-\hat\pi)^2}
&& \text{evaluate at }\pi=\hat\pi \\[6pt]
&= \frac{N\hat\pi}{\hat\pi^2} + \frac{N(1-\hat\pi)}{(1-\hat\pi)^2}
&& \text{use }k=N\hat\pi,\; N-k=N(1-\hat\pi) \\[6pt]
&= N\!\left(\frac{1}{\hat\pi} + \frac{1}{1-\hat\pi}\right)
&& \text{cancel a factor in each term} \\[6pt]
&= N\!\left(\frac{\hat\pi+(1-\hat\pi)}{\hat\pi(1-\hat\pi)}\right)
&& \text{use }\tfrac{1}{a}+\tfrac{1}{b}=\tfrac{a+b}{ab} \\[6pt]
&= \frac{N}{\hat\pi(1-\hat\pi)}
&& \text{simplify}
\end{align*}
:::


\newpage

## Delta Method

We often report odds

$$
\tau(\pi)=\frac{\pi}{1-\pi},
\qquad
\widehat{\text{odds}}=\tau(\hat\pi)=\frac{\hat\pi}{1-\hat\pi}.
$$

### Finding the derivative of $\tau(\pi)$

For the delta method, we need the derivative of $\tau{\pi}$.

$$
\tau'(\pi) = \frac{1}{(1-\pi)^2}.
$$


::: callout-note
## Some tedious algebra

\begin{align*}
\tau(\pi) &= \frac{\pi}{1-\pi} \\[6pt]
\tau'(\pi) &= \frac{1\cdot(1-\pi) - \pi\cdot(-1)}{(1-\pi)^2}
&& \text{quotient rule} \\[6pt]
&= \frac{1-\pi+\pi}{(1-\pi)^2}
= \frac{1}{(1-\pi)^2}.
&& \text{combine terms}
\end{align*}
:::

\newpage

### Plugging into the delta method equation

Recall that $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}\big(\tau(\hat\theta)\big)\;\approx\;\big(\tau'(\hat\theta)\big)^2\,\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat\theta)$.

Applying this, we obtain

$$
\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}\!\big(\widehat{\text{odds}}\big) \approx \frac{\hat\pi}{N(1-\hat\pi)^3}.
$$

Taking the square root,

$$
\boxed{\ \widehat{\mathrm{SE}}\!\big(\widehat{\text{odds}}\big)
= \sqrt{\tfrac{\hat\pi}{N(1-\hat\pi)^3}}\ }.
$$

::: callout-note
## Some tedious algebra

\begin{align*}
\small
\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}\!\big(\widehat{\text{odds}}\big)
  &\approx \Big(\tau'(\hat\pi)\Big)^2\,\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat\pi)
  && \text{delta method} \\[6pt]
  &= \left(\frac{1}{(1-\hat\pi)^2}\right)^{\!2}\;\cdot\;\frac{\hat\pi(1-\hat\pi)}{N}
  && \text{use }\ \tau'(\pi)=\dfrac{1}{(1-\pi)^2},\ \ \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat\pi)=\dfrac{\hat\pi(1-\hat\pi)}{N} \\[6pt]
  &= \frac{1}{(1-\hat\pi)^4}\;\cdot\;\frac{\hat\pi(1-\hat\pi)}{N}
  && \text{square the derivative} \\[6pt]
  &= \frac{\hat\pi}{N(1-\hat\pi)^3}
  && \text{cancel one factor of }(1-\hat\pi)\text{ and rearrange}
\end{align*}
:::
